outcomes: A CLI run is unaffected by whether this receiver is fast, slow, broken, or unreachable
An operator answers aggregate product questions without any surface that can return a single device's activity
A reader of the public documentation can check what is collected against what this workload actually accepts
nonGoals: Retaining raw events, caller IP addresses, or anything that identifies a user or a workspace
Offering an export, a raw-event read, or any per-device query
Promising availability or retention for the hosted service
Governing telemetry inside applications built with the Go or TypeScript frameworks

requirements.text: Ingest accepts no credential and cannot be authenticated: a bearer token on the ingest route is ignored and never drives a key fetch.

The aggregate read denies every request unless issuer, audience, and caller allowlist are all configured and satisfied, and the trailing-slash form of the path is authenticated exactly like the declared path.
A caller's network address is used only to apply request limits and is never stored with an event or an aggregate.
A record is reduced to the compiled field allowlist and closed vocabularies before anything is stored; unknown command names and unknown fields are dropped rather than persisted.
An accepted ingest answers identically whether the payload had content problems or downstream storage was unavailable, so a sender learns nothing about the receiver's internal state.
An aggregate group is withheld unless enough distinct rotating identifiers contributed to it, and repeating an event does not increase that contributor count.
Every business field the CLI sends is folded into a bounded aggregate: project and job counts and session duration only as fixed ranges, flags only as presence counts, never as exact values.
A dimension that reaches its storage ceiling is reported as unavailable rather than returned as a plausible partial count, and unaffected dimensions stay available.
Retention expiry is scheduled in the database so it still runs when the receiver has scaled to zero.
The committed route artifact is byte-identical to what the running server describes, is independent of deploy-time configuration, and declares every path and method the workload serves.
A request outside the declared surface never reaches workload logic, and the receiver never answers a request with a redirect.
